description: Issue #867 (PR #884 cross-vendor review round 2, finding 1): reverts RequestBindingPolicy.IsPathAllowed's zero-resolution handling from `return false;` back to `break;` (src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core/Helper/RequestBindingPolicy.cs), reproducing the exact pre-fix bug the review found: when an intermediate segment fails to resolve (members.Length == 0), `break` exits the foreach loop and falls through to the trailing `return true;`, silently allowing the whole key. This was hidden by a comment claiming 'SetPropertyValue's own traversal would stop (middle hop) or no-op (final hop) too' -- which is false. PropertyHelper.SetPropertyValue's own intermediate loop (PropertyHelper.cs:523-551) ALSO `break`s on a middle-segment miss, but it does not reset tempType/temp -- they stay at whatever they were before the failed hop (the original source, for a first-segment miss) -- and execution falls through to resolve and WRITE the final segment against that frozen type (PropertyHelper.cs:553-559). Checked against RequestBindingPolicyTests867.IsPathAllowed_MissingIntermediateSegmentThenStaticFinal_ReturnsFalse ('Missing.StaticSecret' -- 'Missing' doesn't resolve on FixtureVM, but 'StaticSecret' does and IS static) and IsPathAllowed_MissingIntermediateSegmentThenAmbiguousFinal_ReturnsFalse ('Missing.Label' against AmbiguousShadowVM, where 'Label' is ambiguous) -- the exact two regression shapes the review asked for. With the guard reverted, both return true instead of false, which is what turns the assertions red. The green control, IsPathAllowed_SearcherDotCustomFilterField_ReturnsTrue, exercises a path where every segment resolves cleanly and is genuinely unaffected by this mutant.
target_symbol: RequestBindingPolicy.IsPathAllowed(Type, string, string) -- the zero-resolution `return false;` (originally `break;`) inside `if (members.Length == 0) { ... }`
red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured against a clean checkout with the mutant patch applied (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first): both red tests failed with 'Assert.IsFalse failed.' (neither test has a custom message, so this is the full MSTest failure text for both). Confirmed via python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant wtmsec867-zero-resolution-guard-neutralize: 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS'.
